sentences.text: Monica Seles -LRB- -LSB- ˈsɛləs -RSB- Szeles Mónika , Моника Селеш , Monika Seleš , -LSB- ˈsɛlɛʃ -RSB- , born December 2 , 1973 -RRB- is a former Yugoslav world no. 1 professional tennis player and a member of the International Tennis Hall of Fame .	Yugoslav	Yugoslavia	world no. 1	List of WTA number 1 ranked players	International Tennis Hall of Fame	International Tennis Hall of Fame
An ethnic Hungarian , she was born and raised in Novi Sad , SFR Yugoslavia .	Novi Sad	Novi Sad	SFR Yugoslavia	SFR Yugoslavia	Hungarian	Hungarians
She became a naturalized American citizen in 1994 and also received Hungarian citizenship in June 2007 .	Hungarian	Hungarians	American citizen	American citizen

She won nine Grand Slam singles titles , eight of them while a citizen of Yugoslavia and the final as a citizen of the United States of America .	Grand Slam	Grand Slam (tennis)	United States of America	United States of America
In 1990 , Seles became the youngest-ever French Open champion at the age of 16 .	1990	1990 WTA Tour Championships	French Open	1990 French Open

She went on to win eight Grand Slam singles titles before her 20th birthday and was the year-end world no. 1 in 1991 and 1992 .	1991	1991 Hopman Cup	1992	1992 WTA Tour Championships	world no. 1	List of WTA number 1 ranked players	Grand Slam	Grand Slam (tennis)

However , on April 30 , 1993 , she was the victim of an on-court attack , when a man stabbed her in the back with a 9 in long knife ; Seles did not return to tennis for over two years .	1993	1993 Australian Open – Women's Singles

Though she enjoyed some success after rejoining the tour in 1995 , including a fourth Australian Open title in 1996 , she was unable to consistently reproduce her best form .	1996	1996 Fed Cup	Australian Open	1996 Australian Open
She played her last professional match at the 2003 French Open , but did not officially retire until February 2008 .	French Open	1990 French Open	2003 French Open	2003 French Open

Regarded by many in the sport as one of the greatest tennis players of all time , Seles was named one of the `` 30 Legends of Women 's Tennis : Past , Present and Future '' by Time .	Time	Time (magazine)
